items.title: 5.13.2 Uses of liquid crystals in daily life

source_refs.note: Topic 5.13.2, printed pages 112-113, with Quick Check 5.9 (c) as the self-check. The chapter exercise (pages 113-116) is not reproduced.

blocks.text: The main application area of liquid crystals is electro-optic devices, electrically controlled devices that modulate light in a desired way. Liquid crystals have many uses in daily life.

items: Diagnostics: special liquid crystal devices diagnose tumours and infections in the human body, because physical problems such as tumours often have a different temperature from the surrounding tissue. When cholesteric liquid crystals are applied to the breast, a tumour is located because it is warmer than the other parts; the technique diagnoses breast cancer at an early stage.

Finding characteristic higher temperatures: liquid crystal temperature sensors find faulty connections on a circuit board by detecting their higher temperature, and are used as temperature sensors in thermometers.
Liquid crystal displays (LCDs): the most common application, in oscillographs, televisions, laptops, cell phone displays, computer screens, calculators and watches.

blocks.text: As new properties and types of liquid crystals are investigated, these materials are sure to gain increasing importance in industrial and scientific applications.

blocks.prompt: Which property of liquid crystals makes them usable in temperature-sensing devices?
blocks.explanation: Their optical properties change with temperature: the colour or light transmitted by a cholesteric liquid crystal shifts as it warms or cools, so a thin layer shows a warmer spot (a tumour or a faulty connection) as a change of colour.

items: Uses: diagnosing tumours and infections by temperature (cholesteric crystals on the breast), locating hot faulty connections and acting as thermometers, and LCD screens in televisions, laptops, phones, calculators and watches.
